summary: Master EMR implementation and change management with practical tools, rollout planning, and adoption controls. Enroll to build your implementation capability.
lede: Electronic medical records implementation training helps project, informatics, health information, and operations teams plan a controlled rollout and support adoption. It covers workflow and data-readiness mapping, role-based access and configuration priorities, stakeholder communications, migration and cutover planning, and post-launch adoption tracking. Learners also practice creating readiness profiles, go-live checklists, and stabilization dashboards, while considering interoperability, privacy safeguards, and governance.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for people who help plan, configure, support, or govern an EMR implementation. It is most relevant when you need to translate clinical and administrative requirements into a workable rollout plan, a controlled go-live, and measurable adoption after launch. EHR project managers coordinating EMR rollout tasks and dependencies. Clinical informatics specialists aligning system build with care workflows. Health information managers overseeing documentation integrity and release processes. Practice operations supervisors managing front-office and scheduling impacts. Superusers supporting end-user adoption and issue escalation. Nursing informatics coordinators adapting bedside workflows to the EMR. Physician practice administrators monitoring rollout readiness and service continuity. Revenue cycle analysts tracking documentation and charge capture impacts. Compliance and privacy officers reviewing access and consent controls. IT application support analysts resolving configuration, testing, and cutover issues.
modules: EHR Implementation Readiness and Change Context
prerequisites: You should bring a laptop, a working knowledge of clinical, administrative, or health information workflows, and a willingness to review sample EMR implementation artefacts. Familiarity with EHR terminology, basic privacy principles, and team-based change projects will help you move faster during exercises.
